questions.question: Which best describes the concept "equation mx+b" as taught in the lecture?
options: It is the formula for the regression (best‑fit) line that relates the X and Y quantities in a linear relationship.
It is used to calculate the slope of a parabola.
It is the equation for a circle in Cartesian coordinates.
It represents the area under the curve of the data points.
questions.distractor_a: It represents the area under the curve of the data points.
questions.distractor_b: It is used to calculate the slope of a parabola.
questions.distractor_c: It is the equation for a circle in Cartesian coordinates.

questions.question: Which best describes 'simple linear regression concepts' as taught in the lecture?
options: Simple linear regression models the relationship between a single predictor and a response variable using a straight line, estimating the slope and intercept that minimize the sum of squared residuals.
The model assumes a nonlinear relationship between predictor and response.
It estimates the mean of the response variable without considering any predictors.
Simple linear regression uses multiple predictors to model the response variable.
questions.distractor_a: It estimates the mean of the response variable without considering any predictors.
questions.distractor_b: Simple linear regression uses multiple predictors to model the response variable.
questions.distractor_c: The model assumes a nonlinear relationship between predictor and response.

questions.question: Which best describes 'simple linear regression' as taught in the lecture?
options: It uses a polynomial equation to model the relationship between X and Y.
It is the process of drawing a best‑fit line through plotted X and Y points, whose equation is of the form y = mx + b, where m and b are determined from the data.
It requires transforming Y into a logarithmic scale before fitting.
It is a method for predicting future values of X based on Y.
questions.distractor_a: It uses a polynomial equation to model the relationship between X and Y.
questions.distractor_b: It is a method for predicting future values of X based on Y.
questions.distractor_c: It requires transforming Y into a logarithmic scale before fitting.

questions.question: Which best describes 'multiple linear regression' as taught in the lecture?
options: It requires that all independent variables be categorical.
Multiple linear regression uses a single independent variable to predict a dependent variable.
Multiple linear regression models a dependent variable as a linear combination of two or more independent variables, estimating coefficients that minimize the sum of squared residuals.
It is only applicable when the dependent variable follows a normal distribution.
questions.distractor_a: Multiple linear regression uses a single independent variable to predict a dependent variable.
questions.distractor_b: It requires that all independent variables be categorical.
questions.distractor_c: It is only applicable when the dependent variable follows a normal distribution.

questions.question: Which best describes the "regression line" as taught in the lecture?
options: It is a curve that represents the exact relationship between X and Y.
It is the best‑fit straight line drawn through plotted X and Y points, whose equation is of the form y = mx + b.
It is a vertical line that indicates the mean of X values.
It is a line that shows the average value of Y for each X.
questions.distractor_a: It is a line that shows the average value of Y for each X.
questions.distractor_b: It is a curve that represents the exact relationship between X and Y.
questions.distractor_c: It is a vertical line that indicates the mean of X values.
